I’ve been having these flashbacks—really vivid, like I’m back there. Out of nowhere, I’ll remember the crash: the headlights, the sound of metal twisting. I can’t shut it out. Some mornings I wake up drenched in sweat, heart pounding, not sure where I am. It’s been happening since the accident—though I honestly couldn’t tell you if it’s been weeks or months. Time’s been a blur.  

Driving used to be my thing—kept me independent, you know? Now I don’t even care if I pick up fares. I used to take pride in my work, staying sharp, saving up. Not anymore. What’s the point?  

And it wasn’t my fault—that truck ran the light. They should’ve been paying attention. I keep seeing it, hearing the horn, then—*snap*—I’m flinching, sometimes jerking the wheel. Loud noises wreck me. A backfire, a siren—I jump like I’ve been shocked. My head feels thick, like I’m moving through water. Can’t focus long enough to plan my route. Fear’s just… always there. Low. Constant. Like something bad’s about to happen again.  

I just want to feel normal behind the wheel. But I don’t even know what normal is right now.
D018-D019_h001.question_a:
I’ve been having a hard time since that nighttime fare last February—guy got violent, pulled a knife, made me drive at gunpoint. Even though it’s been over four months now, I keep seeing it like it’s happening all over again. Outta nowhere, I’ll be stuck in traffic or clocking in for a shift, and boom—I’m back in that car, heart pounding, hands shaking.  

The worst part is the noise. Every honk, every slamming door? I jolt like I’ve been shocked. Sometimes I even flinch so hard I drop my keys. My thoughts feel foggy, like I’m walking through thick air. I can’t focus, can’t remember streets I’ve driven for years.  

I don’t care about work like I used to. Used to hustle extra shifts, save a bit—now, what’s the point? I just need to get through the day. And that guy who put me in that situation… it wasn’t just him. The dispatcher knew he was late at night, wouldn’t check in. Feels like they all left me hanging.  

I’m always on edge, like something’s about to go wrong. It’s not just anxiety—it’s constant, like my body won’t calm down. And it’s been like this since March. Not just a few weeks. Longer. Every day feels like I’m still in that car.
D018-D019_h001.question_b:
I’ve been driving a cab for over 20 years, so I’ve seen some things—but nothing like what happened last week. A drunk driver ran a red light and slammed into my passenger side. I wasn’t badly hurt, but I keep seeing it—the lights, the glass shattering, the sound. It just pops into my head when I’m driving, even when I don’t want it to.  

Since then, I jump at every little noise—a car horn, a door slam—I flinch hard, sometimes swerve. My head feels foggy, like I’m moving through water. I can’t focus on traffic signs or remember routes I’ve driven a million times. I’m scared all the time, even when I’m at home. I thought I’d bounce back, but I don’t care about saving for a new car or getting that bonus—things that used to matter. It’s all pointless now. I keep thinking, it should’ve been *him* who got hurt, not me. He was the one drinking. Why should I be the one paying?  

It’s only been ten days since the crash. I’m trying to pull it together, but it’s like I’m stuck in that moment. I just want to feel normal behind the wheel again.

I used to love gardening—had the most beautiful roses on the block—but these days, I can’t even stand being outside when the wind picks up. That storm last April… the tornado warning, the basement, the way the house groaned like it was alive… I still feel it in my bones. When someone touches my shoulder unexpectedly, I flinch so hard I’ve knocked things over. My heart pounds, my hands go cold—it’s like I’m back in that basement, frozen, feeling the walls shake.

I don’t enjoy much anymore. Used to knit for the grandchildren, but now it feels pointless. I keep thinking, *If the neighbors had warned us sooner, if they’d taken the threat seriously*, instead of waiting—why didn’t they say something? That moment—the deafening roar, the sheer terror—plays in my head like a broken record. I can’t clear the fog in my thoughts; I forget what I came into a room for, or lose track of time.

It’s been over six months now. I thought I’d regain myself, but it’s only gotten worse. The fear doesn’t fade—it’s still right here.

My chest tightens, my hands shake. It feels like I’m right back there.

I used to love gardening, baking for the seniors’ group… but now, I don’t see the point. Can’t focus long enough to follow a recipe. My thoughts feel foggy, like I’m moving through water. And it’s not me—it’s *him*. That man stole more than my purse. He stole my peace. This happened just two weeks ago, so I know it’s fresh, but I’m scared it won’t get better.

I can’t relax, not really. Even at home, with the locks checked and the lights off, I feel like I’m listening, waiting. It’s exhausting. I know logically I’m safe, but my body doesn’t seem to get that message.
